PullRequest.Title: agentHost: keep the CLI session's effort and context size on /code
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #346919

When `/code` opens a Copilot CLI session in VS Code on a cold start, the chat restored only the session's model. The effort and context size fell back to VS Code's saved preferences, for example Claude Opus 5.5 · High · 200K showed as Medium · 1M. The next turn from VS Code then sent those values and changed the CLI session.

- **Restore:** the chat keeps the configuration of the imported draft (new `transferredState.selectedModelConfiguration`) along with its model, while the model list is still loading.
- **Model configuration report:** the per-chat report now matches models that the runtime attributes to the `copilot` provider, which the catalog lists by their bare id. A session without a context tier is reported as the default (smallest) window, which is the tier the runtime runs it on. The import's selection does the same.
- **Configuration store:** in a chat with turns, the values the runtime reports win over preferences the chat inherited but never set. Values picked or restored in the chat stay as they are.

Nothing new waits: the configuration arrives with the draft and the existing report.

## How to test

1. In the Copilot CLI, pick Claude Opus 5.5 with High effort and the 200K context window, and send a message.
2. With VS Code closed, run `/code`.
3. The Chat view shows Claude Opus 5.5 · High · 200K. Send a message, then check the session in the CLI: it still runs with High effort and the default context tier.

## Validation

- `scripts\test.bat` for `chatModelConfigurationStore`, `copilotManagedModelConfiguration`, `copilotAgent` and `chatService`: **passed** (1496 passing). The four new tests fail without the fix.
- `scripts\test.bat` for `newChatWidget`, `sessionModelSelection`, `sessionComparisonModelSelection`, `modelPickerActionItem`, `agentHostChatContribution`, `chatContinueInCopilotAction`, `copilotAgentSession` and `agentService`: **passed** (4598 passing, 16 pending).
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` and `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files: **passed**.
- The steps above, end to end on Windows with a dev build and CLI 1.0.109: **passed**. VS Code showed High · 200K (before: VS Code's saved preference, e.g. 1M), and the turn sent from VS Code ran with High effort and the default context tier.
- Cold-start time to show the session, with alternating builds and a new CLI session each run: no change (median from window to restored turns: 3756 ms before, 3743 ms after; 3 runs each).

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold-opening an existing Copilot CLI chat through /code and restoring its draft model configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing session and chat subscriptions must hydrate, history must be restored, and the remote chat model must publish before the chat is usable. The diff only reads the already-hydrated draft model config and carries the same small object into intended-model state; it adds no await or boundary to this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Hydrate the existing backend session and chat subscriptions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one session-channel and one chat-channel hydration for a cold open; existing subscriptions can be reused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same session and chat subscriptions were hydrated and awaited; the draft's model configuration was simply not retained in transferredState.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both hydrations are already on the cold-open critical path before draft and history conversion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the chat-session provider content via getOrCreateChatSession.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider load per session resource after coalescing concurrent consumers; zero on a warm cached-model hit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider was resolved with the same cardinality; only the local transferred-state fields consumed afterward differ.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider resolution is on the cold-open critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: History size controls pre-existing replay/conversion work, while the added selectedModelConfiguration has only the model's bounded picker keys and is retained once per open session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Session and chat hydration are awaited sequentially as before. ChatService coalesces concurrent loads per session resource in _remoteSessionLoads, and warm opens reuse the existing model.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A warm open acquires the existing ChatModel. Cold concurrent opens are coalesced by session resource; canceled loads are sequenced before retry. The added configuration has no cache or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed lines perform direct property reads and retain/pass one bounded configuration object after existing hydration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact subscription latency and history size vary, but the diff does not add calls, waits, history scans, or copies proportional to history.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The critical-path boundaries and their cardinality are unchanged, and the added local work is constant and small.

Scenarios.Scenario: Importing/resuming a Copilot CLI session and deriving the picker selection from the runtime model tier
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing in-use check, optional bounded release polling, session resume, mode adoption, and runtime-selection read must complete before import returns. The diff adds a model-catalog lookup and filtering only when the runtime context tier is unset.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check whether the SDK session is in use, potentially poll, resume the session, adopt modes, and read runtime selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial checkInUse call, a bounded number of retry checks only while another client still holds the session, and one runtime selection read for a successful import.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same calls and sequencing occurred; an unset context tier skipped only the subsequent local context-window derivation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing RPCs are on the import critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The newly reached local work scans the loaded model catalog once and filters one model's small context-size enum; it does not scale with history, turns, or sessions beyond one execution per import.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Import work is serialized by the existing per-chat queue/sequencer. Release polling is sequential and capped by IMPORT_SESSION_RELEASE_POLLS.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing Copilot client and resolved chat session are reused when available. If model metadata is not loaded, the helper returns undefined without retries or new boundary work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: _contextSizeForTier now reaches _contextSizeWindows for an unset tier, which performs one Array.find and one small enum filter with no I/O.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog size can vary, but it is a bounded UI model catalog and this work occurs once per explicit import, not per token, turn item, or frame.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added O(model-catalog-size) local lookup is low-frequency and bounded, while all RPC cardinality remains unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refreshing and displaying a running session's managed model configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A refresh resolves managed settings, lists runtime models, reads the current model, builds a report, publishes changed session configuration, and reactively updates the chat input picker. The diff changes provider-id matching, default-tier projection, and key precedence but does not schedule another refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve managed settings and invoke session.model.list plus session.model.getCurrent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One settings resolution, one model-list RPC, and one current-model RPC per pre-existing refresh trigger; queued refreshes execute serially and stale generations do not publish.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same refresh triggers and RPC sequence existed; the report could fail to match a Copilot-provider current model and omitted contextSize for an unset tier.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations gate configuration-report publication but are not newly placed on chat rendering or message-send paths by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compare and publish the per-chat model configuration through session config state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one publication per materially changed report; equal reports are suppressed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same report object was compared and published; the changed report contains at most a few additional primitive config fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Publication drives a reactive picker update after the RPC refresh completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Report construction remains O(number of catalog models times the three supported option keys). UI application remains O(reported model IDs times schema/default keys). The changed current config adds only bounded primitive fields.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refreshes are serialized through _modelConfigurationRefresh; a generation check drops stale results. Publishing is deep-equality guarded, and ChatModelConfigurationStore also ignores equal reports.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Equal reports are suppressed both before session-config publication and in the UI store. Warm unchanged reports therefore do not retrigger reconciliation; failures publish undefined as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: callers, sequencer, generation guard, equality checks, and reactive consumer were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Model catalog size varies, but effective option cardinality is fixed at three and no changed line increases refresh frequency or boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing boundary work remains serialized and deduplicated; additional report data and local reconciliation are bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Applying a runtime configuration report to a started chat whose inherited preferences were never explicitly selected
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A reactive session-report change synchronously reconciles model configurations and fires one batched change event before the picker rerenders.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing reconciliation scales with the union of override and reported model IDs and each model's schema keys. The diff adds one _ownKeys lookup and, only when absent, an empty Set allocation for the current model's runtime application.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The UI update runs synchronously on one report notification, but equal reports return early and all affected model IDs are notified in one event.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Deep equality suppresses unchanged snapshots. The configuration store keeps per-model overrides and own-key sets for the editor lifetime; the new fallback Set is temporary and not retained.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed branch and all call sites were inspected; there is no new boundary, listener, per-frame path, or unbounded retention.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Report frequency depends on runtime configuration changes, but unchanged reports are suppressed upstream and locally.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extra synchronous work is constant per affected current model and remains behind existing report deduplication.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and traced cold restore/import, runtime report refresh, and UI reconciliation. No diff-introduced performance regression met the reporting threshold; no finding or regression-fix record was submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
